title: the records tell the truth: the promise of the claim, the numbers of the waves
intent: The wave repairs the truth of the records and the promise of the claim of the wave 98.  (1) **The promise of the claim is narrowed to what is measured.**  The claim `a-tool-declares-its-own-risk' promised that the profiles name exactly the tools the measurement found, while the measurement finds ten tools that change the world and the profile `plan' names nine of them in the context of the check -- `bridge__eval' registers itself through `yeah-bridge-register' only (`lib/yeah-bridge.el:254'), and the filter by the registry dropped it from the comparison; the clause of the falsifier was literally satisfied and the check did not see it.  The text and the falsifier of the claim are amended -- the text says that the profiles name exactly the tools the measurement found **among the tools the registry holds**, and the falsifier names three refusals -- while the `id', the `requirements' and the `control' of the claim are the same.  (2) **The header of the check is brought into agreement with the measurement.**  The fifth item of the header says that the profiles name exactly the tools of the measurement that the registry holds, an added paragraph says why the comparison is over the registry (the rule asks by the declarations of the registry, and the tool of the bridge is not named by the profile while the bridge has not registered it), and the refusals name `the tools of the registry that change the world'.  (3) **A stand says that the comparison bites.**  The comparison moved into `yeah-check--profile-mismatch' and the selection of the measured tools into `yeah-check--mutating-tools', and two stands forge a profile that names a tool the measurement does not find and a measurement that does not hold a tool that changes the world -- both must be refused, so a comparison that accepts everything falls on the stands.  (4) **The numbers of the wave 97 are a snapshot and not the present.**  `docs/PLAN.md' and `AGENTS.md' named `lib/' as 66 modules with 64 named and the breakdown of the definitions as 52 `defun', 5 `defconst', 5 `cl-defun' and 2 `cl-defstruct' as if they were the present, while the numbers of the names were marked as historical; now they are marked as the snapshot of the wave 97 (the commit `5c12b65').  (5) **The numbers of the comparison of the 64 names are the measured ones.**  61 of the 64 names hold the same definition on the same line, 3 left and were re-anchored to the same definition with the very same text of the form, and no definition changed its signature.  (6) **The numbers of the waves 101 and 102 are the measured ones.**  `lib/yeah-proc.el' holds 5 961 bytes and not 5 966, the check of the wave 101 holds 14 035 bytes and not 14 043, and the check of the wave 102 holds 343 lines and not 340; the first two were right before the commit `8a22cf3' and the third before `99958b8', and both commits are ancestors of the commits of the records, so the numbers were stale already when they were written.  (7) **A finding of the parent (F53).**  The record of the wave 101 named `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md' §2.1, and there is no such heading -- the headings of the file are `§1' to `§11' with `§11.1' to `§11.17' -- and the guard of the documentation does not read `waves/*.json' at all, so it could not see the name.  The wave touches no code of the kernel except the check of the wave 98, and it is a wave of the records.
objection: The wave touches no kernel, and its price is named.  (a) **The promise is narrower after the wave than before it**: the claim of the wave 98 promised that the profiles name exactly the tools the measurement found, and now it promises that they name the tools the measurement found among the tools the registry holds; the part that the bridge leaves out is named in the text of the claim and in the falsifier, but the claim is weaker than it was.  (b) **The measurement of the registry is a fact of the moment**: a tool that the registry holds after the snapshot is not named by the profile, and the check of the wave says so -- the extension that compares the profile with the profile plus the tools registered after the snapshot is a possible next step, and it is not part of this wave.  (c) **The stand of the comparison is a stand of the check itself**: it forges a profile and a measurement inside the check, so it proves that the comparison of the check bites, and not that the rule of the kernel is right -- the rule is proven by the other five items of the check.  (d) **The numbers are of two kinds**: the numbers of the wave 97 are a snapshot and cannot be true today, and the numbers of the waves 101 and 102 are a measurement and are true today; the wave does not make them one kind.  (e) **The guard of the documentation does not read the records of the waves**: the name of a section that is not there lived in `waves/*.json' for a wave and nobody saw it, and the wave fixes that one name and names the hole, but does not close it -- the closing of the hole is a wave of its own, and the decision about the price of that wave is the owner's.
note: The wave is the truth of the records, and every number of it was measured.  (1) **What the wave repaired.**  Four findings of the discriminator of the package of the waves 97 to 100 (F40, F41, F42) and one finding of the discriminator of the package of the waves 101 to 103 (F50), and one finding of the parent (F53).  (2) **The code.**  `tests/checks/check-a-tool-declares-its-own-risk.el' -- 1 183 lines and 52 744 bytes, it was 1 129 lines and 49 546 bytes; the comparison of the fifth measurement is now a named function `yeah-check--profile-mismatch' over the named selection `yeah-check--mutating-tools', and the refusal reads `the %s profile names %S, but the tools of the registry that change the world are %S'.  The check of the wave passes with the code 0 on the honest tree, and the stands of the comparison pass with it.  (3) **The claim.**  The claim `a-tool-declares-its-own-risk' keeps its `id', its `scope', its `requirements', its `kind', its `phase', its `owner', its `register' and its `control'; its TEXT names the tools the registry holds, and its FALSIFIER names three refusals where it named one.  (4) **The numbers, measured.**  `lib/yeah-proc.el' -- 127 lines and 5 961 bytes; `tests/checks/check-a-process-that-is-dead-is-dead-everywhere.el' -- 296 lines and 14 035 bytes; `tests/checks/check-the-tree-of-the-processes-survives-a-vanished-process.sh' -- 343 lines; `tests/checks/check-a-tool-declares-its-own-risk.el' -- 1 183 lines and 52 744 bytes.  (5) **The snapshot of the wave 97.**  The commit `5c12b65' holds the state in which `lib/' held 66 modules with 64 named, and in which the names of the picture were 52 `defun', 5 `defconst', 5 `cl-defun' and 2 `cl-defstruct'.  (6) **The comparison of the 64 names.**  Measured against the snapshot of the wave 97: 61 names hold the same definition on the same line, 3 left their line and were re-anchored to the same definition with the very same text of the form (`lib/yeah-perm.el' 62 to 68, `lib/yeah-tools.el' 118 to 119, `lib/yeah-delegate.el' 428 to 430), and 0 of the 64 definitions changed its signature.  (7) **The hole the wave names and does not close.**  The guard `tests/checks/check-the-documentation-points-at-files-that-exist.el' reads `docs/*.md', `AGENTS.md', `README.md' and `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md', and it does not read `waves/*.json' -- the records of the waves are the records of the truth, and the guard of the truth does not read them.  (8) **The live route.**  No live run was made for this wave: it touches no code of the kernel except a check, and the live route of the package of the waves 101 to 103 is the open finding F49 of that package.
